findings.title: get_workout_stats counts never-ended (in-progress/abandoned) workouts as zero-duration, deflating average duration and skewing distribution
findings.description: In get_workout_stats the base CTE `workout_times` selects FROM workouts with only `WHERE user_id = ?` and no `end_time > start_time` filter (lines 411-420). A freshly created workout is stored with end_time == start_time (server/src/db/workouts.rs:82-93, INSERT sets end_time = start_time), and a workout that is abandoned and never ended stays that way indefinitely when auto-close is disabled (inactivity_minutes <= 0, server/src/main.rs schedule_auto_close). For those rows `ROUND((julianday(end_time)-julianday(start_time))*24*60)` = 0. `total_workouts` (line 492) counts them, `avg_duration = AVG(duration)` (line 493) averages the zeros in, and `duration_ranges`/`duration_distribution` (lines 473-489) buckets them into '0-30'. This is internally inconsistent: within the SAME function `avg_exercise_duration_series` (line 636) and `session_start_times` (line 689) DO filter `end_time > start_time`, and get_calendar_workout_frequency (progress_consistency.rs:35) also filters `end_time > start_time`, so the frequency stat counts only completed workouts while total_workouts/avg_duration count all. Net effect: the displayed average session duration and duration histogram are wrong (dragged toward 0) whenever a user has any open or abandoned workout.
findings.attackOrTrigger: Any authenticated web or MCP user hits GET /api/stats (services::progress::get_workout_stats -> db.get_workout_stats) while having an in-progress workout, or after abandoning workouts with auto-close disabled. No special input needed; the more open/abandoned sessions, the more the average duration and the 0-30min bucket are skewed downward.
findings.why: Reported statistics are silently incorrect, not a security issue. No data loss or escalation, but a real user-facing numeric correctness bug in a launch-facing dashboard.
findings.fixSketch: Add `AND end_time > start_time` to the `workout_times` CTE (or exclude zero/near-zero durations from avg_duration, total_workouts-for-duration, and duration_ranges) so the duration statistics only consider completed workouts, matching the other series in the same function and get_calendar_workout_frequency.

findings.title: PR / recent-best detection groups by exact-case exercise_type while volume/records pages match case-insensitively, producing split and inconsistent PR streams
findings.description: detect_pr_events and detect_recent_best_events key their running-best maps on the raw `fact.exercise_type` string (HashMap<String,...> at lines 95-99 and format!("{}::...", fact.exercise_type) at lines 191-238). exercise_type is stored verbatim from the client with no normalization on write (create_exercise inserts req.exercise_type as-is, server/src/db/exercises.rs:41-56). Meanwhile the per-exercise views match case-insensitively: get_exercise_progress uses `LOWER(exercise_type) = LOWER(?)` (line 363) and get_volume_stats uses `LOWER(e.exercise_type) = LOWER(?)` (lines 1079, 1149, 1211, 1241). Consequently, the same exercise logged as e.g. "Bench Press" and "bench press" (or with trailing whitespace) is treated as ONE exercise on the detail/volume/records page but as TWO independent PR histories in the progress overview. This yields recent_prs / pr_count / recent_best_count in get_progress_overview that disagree with the personal_records shown on the exercise page (a lift the user knows is not a PR gets re-flagged as a PR the first time each casing variant appears, and per-period pr_count deltas are inflated).
findings.attackOrTrigger: A user or an MCP agent creates exercises of the same movement with differing casing/whitespace in exercise_type (common when free-typed on web vs. AI-generated names via MCP), then loads GET /api/progress/overview vs. the exercise detail/volume endpoints. The two surfaces report different PRs/records for what is logically the same exercise.
findings.why: Purely a correctness/consistency defect in derived analytics; no security impact and no persisted corruption, hence low severity. Impact is user confusion and slightly inflated PR counts, not data loss.
findings.fixSketch: Normalize the grouping key consistently: lowercase (and trim) fact.exercise_type when building the HashMap keys in detect_pr_events/detect_recent_best_events so it matches the LOWER(...) comparisons used by get_volume_stats/get_exercise_progress; ideally also normalize exercise_type on write in create_exercise so all code paths agree.
